content.text: Continuous-time dynamics and sampled dynamics require an explicit hold convention. For piecewise constant inputs held over a sample period Δ, the exact discrete update is `y[k+1]=a y[k]+b u[k]`, with `a=exp(−Δ/τ)` and `b=K(1−a)`. content.text: Exact model discretization does not identify the actual plant. For piecewise constant inputs held over a sample period Δ, the exact discrete update is `y[k+1]=a y[k]+b u[k]`, with `a=exp(−Δ/τ)` and `b=K(1−a)`. This zero-order-hold conversion follows by integrating the first-order differential equation. It is not the same as Euler approximation `a≈1−Δ/τ`, which can produce misleading behavior at large Δ. MathWorks documents the ZOH convention for conversion of continuous LTI models to sampled systems. A real digital controller also has conversion, sampling jitter, computational latency, quantization, scheduling and delay; none are present in the toy update.
